error_message: [gold priors] eflomal.calculate_priors failed for en: can only concatenate str (not "int") to str
root_cause: A gold record (sentence_id 0, 'lefe texto' <-> 'Preface') carries links [[0,1],[1,2],[0,0],[1,0]] while the stored target has only 1 token, so j=1 and j=2 are out of bounds. eflomal.calculate_priors raises on the first out-of-bounds link, and its own error path is buggy -- `raise ValueError('Invalid input on line %d' % lineno + 1)` evaluates as (str % int) + int, so a TypeError masks the real 'alignment out of bounds' message. Because the bad record was first in the list, ALL 54 gold records were silently discarded (run_giza_improved catches the exception and prints '[gold priors] skipped').
fix: _pharaoh() now takes optional n_src/n_tgt and drops links pointing past either token list, returning (pharaoh_string, dropped_count). append_gold_priors() passes the token counts, logs which sentence_id had out-of-bounds links, and warns that those rows are stale and need re-annotation. Verified: all 54 gold records now yield 364 LEX / 13 HMMF / 14 HMMR / 261 FERF / 271 FERR priors.

error_message: Editing a sense label in the image curator kicks you out of the field the moment you click into it

The label input and PoS select also set the active sense on focus, and their change handlers return early when the value is unchanged, so tabbing through a field no longer triggers a save-and-rebuild.

error_message: Recurring: words whose gloss carries a plain parenthetical after the colon were split into extra part-of-speech slots in the Anki deck (e.g. dento 'that; that one', keto 'what, which; what, which one', lil 'minorly, a little; minorly, a little bit')
root_cause: _parseAnnotatedEnglish always ran _expand_gloss_context, which turns a gloss with a plain (non-italic) parenthetical into TWO readings -- compact and verbose ('ace (card)' -> 'ace', 'ace card'). That expansion exists for sense matching: extending glosses into more languages via Wiktionary and Apertium. But AnkiMaker3 lays each ParsedGloss into a slot of its own, so one gloss consumed two, doubling the text in a slot and silently dropping the parentheses where only the verbose reading survived ('be on top of' for 'be on top (of)').
fix: Threaded an expand_context flag through _parseAnnotatedEnglish. parseEntry -- used only by the Anki makers, which are slot-based -- defaults it to False, so a parenthetical stays intact in one slot. parseWordEntry keeps expanding, so the dictionary, Wiktionary extension and Apertium paths are untouched. 568 of 8879 exported rows corrected.

error_message: Word Selector proposals and cluster order differ between runs of the same concept
root_cause: WiktionaryDB.get_translations returns sets; non-English edition tables were iterated in hash order, so word order (and every order-based tie-break: MSA centre, blend, ranking) changed with PYTHONHASHSEED
fix: sort translations (and language codes) where they are read in sources/wiktionary.table() and field.tables(); verified identical results under seeds 0, 1, 7

error_message: Blending step slow (~15 s), clustering slow with more words
root_cause: LexiliAsel precedent models re-learned (~5000 MSAs over all roots, 13.5 s) in every new server process; distance() recomputed for repeated pairs
fix: precedent models pickled to word_selection_cache/precedent_<group>.pickle keyed on word list + concept index + code fingerprints, warmed at server start; align.distance memoized; two-phase run (prepare/finish) so only ticked clusters are blended

error_message: menalariExtension.tsv and _clarifiers.tsv differ between two runs of the same code (~2,400 diff lines, e.g. abacus (_ferrāmentum_) vs (_instrūmentum_))
root_cause: _resolve_lang built its list by iterating a set of Translation (deserialize_translations returns sets), so the order changed with PYTHONHASHSEED; the builder's extension_words order followed it and Clarifiers._own takes items[0]. bug-231 had sorted only the joins in entry_to_string.
fix: _resolve_lang iterates sorted(...) (the LMDB's stored order); two runs with PYTHONHASHSEED=1 and 2 are byte-identical

error_message: rtx-proc (epo-glb, glb-epo, glb-spa) memory explodes on multi-sentence input: >4 GB for 8 epo sentences, machine went into swap and was rebooted
root_cause: SEQ -> SEQ sent made the sentence end part of a SEQ that every SEQ X rule extends again, so the whole text was one rtx-proc -a parse and the comma/relative ambiguities of each sentence multiplied with the next
fix: SENT -> SEQ sent as a separate top-level rule (SENT: _;) that nothing extends; per-sentence output identical in words (220 sentences changed only quote/blank placement, all corrections), chrF epo-glb 65.87->66.60, glb-epo 56.36->57.05, glb-spa unchanged; 566 sentences at once now 74 MB

error_message: wasm lt-proc orders equally weighted analyses differently from native (deu-glb UDHR: 'kulturali haki' vs native 'kulturali Kanan')
root_cause: std::sort is unstable; above 16 elements libstdc++ (native) and libc++ (Emscripten) introsorts permute ties differently; State::NFinals sorts all analyses by weight
fix: libstdc++'s sort algorithm ported to gnu_sort.hpp and force-included into lttoolbox state.cc and lrx_processor.cc

error_message: RuntimeError: unreachable after apertium-pretransfer / apertium-tagger / cg-proc wrote correct output (wasm multicall)
root_cause: main renamed with -Dmain=x loses C++'s implicit return 0; falling off the end is UB and clang emits unreachable
fix: rename_main.py copies each main source with main renamed and an explicit return 0 before its closing brace

error_message: wasm tools: u_sscanf 'unable to parse int' (apertium-anaphora), lrx weights wrong, rtx 'unable to titlecase'
root_cause: Emscripten's icu port links stub data; ICU formatted I/O and word breaks need locale data; ICU_DATA set after the module started was never seen (libc copies environ in a constructor)
fix: trimmed icudt68l.dat (16 traced items, 0.5 MB) packed by icupkg --ignore-deps, mounted and ICU_DATA set in preRun

error_message: fra-glb in browser: FileNotFoundError for fra-glb.imparfait.json
root_cause: absolute paths in Python-step arguments were not rewritten to /p/... nor copied
fix: rewrite and copy them like tool arguments

error_message: browser translator output shows escapes: \@running, be\@compile (user screenshot)
root_cause: the browser ran the bare mode (as the translation aide does), not the apertium command's plain-text path: no apertium-destxt (input escaping, superblanks), apertium-normalize, wblank-attach/-detach, apertium-retxt (unescaping)
fix: destxt/retxt (xsltproc+flex, -P prefix, rename_main --isolate namespace), normalize, wblank-attach/-detach added to the multicall wasm; manifests from the native apertium-wblank-mode output wrapped in destxt/retxt; SETVAR stream command after destxt, stripped before retxt; nfcn.nrm mounted at /icu; parity reference is now `apertium -d pair mode FILE` (stdin from Node made the wrapper's destxt print its usage)

error_message: eng->glb: 'I totally agree' -> 'Mi totalmodongwi' (adverb glued to verb)
root_cause: VP -> AVP vv { 1 %2 } had no blank between the children
fix: { 1 _ %2 }; prefix adverbs (preflist) keep their own joining rules

error_message: names with inner capitals came out as 'WebAssembly/Webassembly'
root_cause: lt-proc matches the name regex (bidix and generator) twice: as written and case-normalised
fix: bidix side: manfem drops case variants of np translations; generator side: glb-pregen writes ^Name<np>$ as plain text (lt-proc -c would break capitalised ordinary words)

error_message: glb-pregen first version stripped -mo before unknown adjectives (godomo *dangereux -> godo)
root_cause: unknown words have no tags, so 'next is not adj/adv' was true
fix: strip only when the next word is known and of another class or the sentence ends; unknown, participle, comma and ji keep -mo

error_message: coordinated passive rtx rule lost 'le' and the passive (were opened and closed -> Dwer bebuka ji klosido)
root_cause: the new vv rules interfered with tense propagation; second participles were not tagged pp by the rule-only tagger
fix: reverted; coordinated passive left open

root_cause: bidix entry for can<vbmod><past> had a malformed left side 'u<vbpr><cni> abil<vbmod>' (tags inside the lemma)
fix: RL entry abil<vbmod> <- can<vbmod><past>; tense left unmarked as in the gold

error_message: eng-glb CG: rules with (NOT 1* X BARRIER Y) fired almost always
root_cause: In CG-3, NOT with a scanning context and BARRIER asks for some cohort that is not X before the barrier; it does not mean 'no X before Y'
fix: All such tests use NEGATE; the three-nouns rule checks finite verbs (Fin) only

error_message: spa-glb: Te quiero -> Yu vole; le dio su pan al hombre -> #prpers
root_cause: NOM -> prn matched clitic pronouns (clitic read as subject); the ditrans VX rule output 1(CL), which applies CL as an output pattern and strips the clitic's tags
fix: NOM -> prn only without pro/enc (clitic attribute); dative clitics output tas + pronoun marked <dbl>, glb-pregen drops it when a full a-phrase recipient is in the clause

error_message: epo word formation: derived bidix entries missing for short conversions (puri <- pura) and an epo analyser that would not load ('Unsupported transducer type')
root_cause: memo key ignored the recursion depth (a depth-1 None was reused at depth 0); a hand block was inserted before the first marker, which is the one in <pardefs>
fix: memo key (lemma, class, depth); hand entries placed before the section block marker
